facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage rose because earnings fell while debt grew. Reported EBITDA dropped from USD 192.1 million in FY2023 to USD 159.5 million in FY2024 and was USD 163.2 million in FY2025, while total debt grew from USD 667.0 million to USD 735.0 million, taking total debt to EBITDA from 3.47x to 4.50x. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; calculation C80; calculation C81; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage depends on the debt perimeter. Total debt of USD 710.7 million counts finance leases of USD 32.0 million but not floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million or operating lease liabilities of USD 116.0 million. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The best case against a harsher view is the direction since June: leverage fell from 4.91x at June 30, 2026 to 4.65x, and net debt fell from USD 716.4 million at FY2025 to USD 688.9 million. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, total debt is 4.38x and cover is 2.15x. No principal falls due before June 2029 and reported availability is USD 413.5 million. Covenant levels, definitions and tests are not printed for any period from FY2023 to September 30, 2026. Every report states only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants. This restricts covenant headroom, any covenant-based liquidity or default analysis and the debt stack's lender tests; no capacity is inferred. The action that would close it is the executed ABL credit agreement, floor plan credit agreement and indenture. Severity: High. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

Borrowing availability cannot be reconciled to the printed facility limits at September 30, 2026. Management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings while the combined limit less borrowings and letters of credit gives USD 530.9 million, a difference of USD 117.4 million, and the borrowing base is not printed. This restricts the undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity chart and every liquidity measure built on it, which carry the reported figure. The action that would close it is the borrowing base certificate or the credit agreement definitions. Severity: High. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C58; calculation C59; Source readiness (CP-0)

The individual floor plan facilities have no printed carrying value, margin, floor or maturity, and the legal rank of the OEM floor plan facilities and of the finance leases is not stated. These instruments therefore carry Not supplied cells in the instrument table and are left out of the debt stack. This restricts any secured-debt subtotal and the ranking of floor plan claims; the action that would close it is the floor plan credit agreements and the intercreditor agreement. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

This restricts every leverage and cover ratio to a labelled basis; the action that would close it is a covenant EBITDA definition, which no supplied document gives. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C72; calculation C73

The debt perimeter is a choice that moves leverage from 4.65x to 6.78x at September 30, 2026: floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million and operating lease liabilities of USD 116.0 million sit outside Total Debt, which follows the issuer's own debt note. This restricts comparison with issuers that count floor plan debt; the action that would close it is a committee decision on the perimeter, with both measures stated. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 16–20; calculation C86; calculation C67

The maturity ladder at September 30, 2026 is built from the instrument terms in the debt note because the quarterly reports print no maturity table; the last printed table is at December 31, 2025, and it holds principal only in 2029. Finance leases are outside the ladder and appear in the reconciling items. This restricts the ladder to ABL and second lien note principal; the action that would close it is a maturity table in a later report. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 20; calculation C60; calculation C61

Cash income taxes paid are not printed for the 2026 interim periods, so cash tax for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 is not established; the annual reports print it for FY2023 to FY2025. This restricts cash-tax-based cash flow measures for 2026; the action that would close it is the cash flow supplemental disclosure in a later report. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

Printed dashes are carried as Not supplied, not as zero, in these lines and periods: other income in Q3 2025; gain or loss on divestitures in FY2023, FY2024, Q1 2025 and Q3 2026; loss on debt extinguishment in FY2023 and FY2025; debt issuance cost and extinguishment lines in FY2023 and FY2025; acquisitions in FY2024, Q1 2026, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; divestiture proceeds in FY2023, FY2024 and Q1 2025; repurchases of common stock in FY2023, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; common dividends in the 2026 periods; and the foreign exchange effect in FY2023 and Q1 2025. Lines a period's statement does not print are likewise Not supplied. The totals tie without them, which indicates nil. This restricts nothing in the ratios; the action that would close it is the issuer's confirmation that a dash means nil. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–74; 10-Q_2026-03-31_altg_altg-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8

Statements for FY2022, per-share data, share counts and the Q2 discrete quarter are not extracted, and segment assets and segment capital expenditures are not extracted. This restricts the history before FY2023 and the segment return measures; the action that would close it is extraction from the segment note and the FY2024 annual report. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–74, 105–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

Operating measures such as rental fleet utilization and backlog are described in words and not quantified, and the preferred stock's liquidation preference is not printed. This restricts operating trend analysis and the ranking of the preferred claim; the action that would close it is management disclosure of those measures. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 48–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 43

No subsequent event is stated in the latest quarterly report, and events between November 9, 2026 and the November 18, 2026 as-of date cannot be checked from the supplied sources. This restricts the post-balance-sheet adjustments to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for that interval. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The operating model is durable at its core and dependent on suppliers at its edges. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, while new and used equipment sales, 54.43% of revenue, earned a 14.07% margin. Alta is the exclusive distributor of new equipment and replacement parts in substantially all of its territories, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue and the top ten are about 6%, so cash flow is spread across many buyers. The dependency is on the manufacturers: five of them supplied 49% of equipment and parts bought in FY2025, a supplier may terminate a distribution agreement, and OEM finance arms provide floor plan lines that renew each year after a credit review, so one supplier's decision can reach both earnings and liquidity. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 13, 19, 30, 71–72; calculation C1; calculation C5

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings rest on Construction Equipment, and Material Handling is the weaker segment in 2026. Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue and 59.52% of segment Adjusted EBITDA before corporate costs, at a 9.04% margin. In the first nine months of 2026 Material Handling revenue fell 5.94% and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.01%, as new and used equipment sales dropped 11.67%, while Construction Equipment revenue rose 1.02% but its Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.74%. Reported group revenue fell 1.76%, but the issuer's organic revenue, which removes acquired and divested revenue, fell only 1.0%, to USD 1,302.5 million from USD 1,315.0 million, so nearly half of the reported decline comes from sold businesses. Group Adjusted EBITDA was USD 121.6 million against USD 123.8 million a year earlier, a margin of 9.33% in both periods, so the earnings base is flat to slightly lower and gives creditors no growth cushion. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The rental fleet is being shrunk on purpose, which turns fleet assets into cash at the cost of rental income. Management began a fleet optimization in mid-2024 aimed at excess rent-to-sell assets and weak-return classes, cutting rental fleet gross cost by USD 84.3 million from 2024-06-30 to 2025-12-31 and new equipment inventory by USD 51.5 million in FY2025. Rental revenue fell 11.60% in FY2025 and a further 4.38% in the first nine months of 2026, while rental equipment sales rose 18.42%, so part of the cash generated has come from selling fleet, not from earnings growth. Management describes rental rates as stable to slightly positive, but utilization is not quantified, so how far the fleet cuts have outrun demand is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation C4; calculation C8

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder distributions exceeded the cash left after investment in each of the last three years, so they leaned on borrowing; they have been cut back since, but not ended. Common dividends, preferred dividends and repurchases totalled USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025, 28.03% of operating cash flow, while operating cash flow less capital expenditure plus asset-sale proceeds was negative in two years and only USD 3.7 million in the third. The common dividend was halved in 2025 and none is printed for 2026, and repurchases of USD 5.8 million in FY2024 and USD 7.5 million in FY2025 have stopped, with USD 16.7 million of authorization still open. The preferred dividend continues, USD 2.2 million in the first nine months of 2026, despite the deficit. The filings give neither a reason for the changes nor a funding source, so the cut-back is observed, not committed. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Corporate activity has shifted from buying to selling, which helps creditors modestly. Alta states that it completed 17 acquisitions since 2020 and describes its growth strategy as historically built on acquisitions, but cash spent on acquisitions was USD 45.6 million in FY2023 and USD 2.7 million in FY2025, with no acquisition cash printed for FY2024. The FY2023 purchases of Burris and Ault were funded, together with working capital and rental fleet growth, from net borrowing of USD 91.3 million under the ABL facility. Three disposals since May 2025 had sale prices of USD 18.0 million, USD 6.4 million and USD 1.5 million, USD 25.9 million in all, and each was allocated to reduce senior debt. The strategy has not been withdrawn, and pro forma earnings and integration results are not disclosed for any purchase, so a return to acquisitions would be a re-leveraging risk that the filings do not size. facts.text: Overall, Alta presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is borrowing-funded distributions that are now curtailed, which matters because every dollar paid out while cash after investment was negative added to the claims that mature together in 2029 and implies a refinancing that depends on cash flow, not on outside support. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that governance risk is higher than medium is a pattern of paying out cash the business had not generated: distributions of USD 41.6 million over three years, repurchases in loss years, a preferred dividend still paid with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million, and two senior officers holding an interest in a related party that has failed. The strongest case that it is lower is behaviour since mid-2025: common dividends and repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt. The view would worsen on evidence of a holder with control of the vote or a cooperation agreement that favours distributions or a sale, wide restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreements combined with resumed dividends or repurchases, or a further payment to OneH2. It would improve if the proxy statement shows an independent board with no controlling holder, the credit documents block distributions while debt is high, and further quarters pass with no payment beyond the preferred dividend. citations.quote: The strongest case that governance risk is higher than medium is a pattern of paying out cash the business had not generated: distributions of USD 41.6 million over three years, repurchases in loss years, a preferred dividend still paid with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million, and two senior officers holding an interest in a related party that has failed. The strongest case that it is lower is behaviour since mid-2025: common dividends and repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt. The view would worsen on evidence of a holder with control of the vote or a cooperation agreement that favours distributions or a sale, wide restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreements combined with resumed dividends or repurchases, or a further payment to OneH2. It would improve if the proxy statement shows an independent board with no controlling holder, the credit documents block distributions while debt is high, and further quarters pass with no payment beyond the preferred dividend.

facts.text: No new debt was issued in FY2025 or in the first nine months of 2026. The last issue was the USD 500.0 million senior secured second lien notes due 2029-06-01, completed on 2024-06-05 to refinance earlier second lien notes due April 2026, with a USD 6.7 million loss on extinguishment, to reduce variable-rate exposure and to provide liquidity and growth funding. The notes are guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary and secured by second-priority liens on substantially all assets, behind the first-priority liens that secure the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility. At September 30, 2026 USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due in 2029, and the floor plan and ABL facilities together are limited to USD 1,064.5 million. This restricts any view that acquisitions added earnings and the currency and regional exposure of the revenue base; the action that would close it is acquisition disclosures and a geographic revenue note. The liquidation preference, redemption terms and dividend-blocking terms of the Series A preferred are not printed, and the multiemployer pension withdrawal liability is not quantified. This restricts the size and ranking of the preferred claim and of the pension contingent claim; the action that would close it is the certificate of designation and plan administrator estimates. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33, 40, 104–105

Events after the latest quarterly report, signed on 2026-11-09, cannot be checked from the supplied sources, and the latest report states no subsequent event. This restricts the events timeline to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for the interval to the as-of date. Severity: Low. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business profile is adequate: exclusive OEM territories and a spread of customers support an aftermarket-heavy earnings stream, but equipment sales and rental income are cyclical and supplier-dependent. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue and 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue, and Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 organic revenue fell 1.0% and Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.78%, with parts margins down 140 bp and service margins up 150 bp as management cut technician headcount and non-billable labor. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases and their finance arms renew floor plan lines each year, so the core is durable and the edge is exposed to supplier decisions. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is stretched and has risen since FY2023 while earnings fell. Total debt to calculated EBITDA rose from 3.47x at FY2023 to 4.50x at FY2025 and 4.65x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and EBITDA cover of cash interest fell from 3.58x to 2.02x, because EBITDA fell 20.46% to USD 152.8 million and total debt rose 6.55% to USD 710.7 million. Counting floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million as debt lifts leverage to 6.78x, while the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA gives 4.38x; a committee should read 4.65x as the measure consistent with the issuer's debt definition and 6.78x as the conservative bound. At the last twelve months' pace of EBITDA less cash interest and capital expenditure, USD 48.7 million, repaying total debt would take 14.59 years, so deleveraging from cash flow is not a credible route to the 2029 maturity. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was an outflow of USD 16.2 million in FY2023, USD 13.5 million in FY2024 and USD 18.0 million in FY2025, then USD 64.2 million positive over the last twelve months. The USD 82.2 million swing is USD 59.1 million from manufacturer floor plan payables, which moved from a USD 55.4 million outflow in FY2025 to a USD 3.7 million net inflow, and USD 22.5 million from lower capital expenditure, leaving USD 0.6 million for everything else; operating cash flow before floor plan changes was USD 88.4 million in FY2025 and USD 89.0 million in the last twelve months. This sharpens Financial foundation, which stressed the nine-month floor plan inflow of USD 30.8 million: over twelve months the net floor plan change is small, and the gain is the end of FY2025's paydown, not new floor plan borrowing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate until 2029 but cannot retire the 2029 debt, and how much of it is drawable is not established. Cash was USD 21.8 million and management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities combined, up from USD 373.8 million at June 30, 2026 and USD 400.2 million at March 31, 2026 but below USD 424.4 million at FY2025. Printed limits less borrowings and letters of credit imply USD 530.9 million, USD 117.4 million more than reported, and the borrowing base is not printed, so reported availability is the figure to use. Cash plus reported availability covers 62.82% of the USD 692.9 million due in 2029. Management says cash flows, cash and borrowings will be adequate for the foreseeable future, and each one percentage point rise in variable rates would cut annual pre-tax earnings by USD 3.5 million. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing capacity is the central uncertainty, because both main facilities fall due on 2029-06-01 with no equity cushion and no committed sponsor. The USD 192.9 million ABL and the USD 500.0 million second lien notes mature on the same day and are 95.59% of contractual principal including finance leases, so one refinancing, priced on 2028 earnings and market conditions, decides the credit. Equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million, the notes rank behind the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility, and no covenant level, borrowing base or lien capacity is printed, so the lender protections that would shape a refinancing are not established. The debt would normally become current from mid-2028, which is when a delayed refinancing would first show in reported liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C10

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margins are stable but the mix inside them is shifting, and operating leverage is high. The consolidated gross margin was 26.9% for nine months 2026 against 26.8%, operating expenses were flat, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.33% in both periods, helped by service margins of 61.1% after technician headcount cuts. Parts margins fell to 33.1% from 34.5%, rental equipment sales margins fell 450 bp as aged fleet was sold, and healthcare costs rose. From FY2023 to FY2025 revenue fell 2.18% while calculated EBITDA fell 15.04%, so a small revenue miss moves earnings several times as much. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy and governance risk is medium, and recent actions support creditors without committing to them. Distributions of USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025 exceeded the cash left after investment in every year, so they leaned on borrowing; since then the common dividend was halved and stopped, repurchases stopped and disposal proceeds of USD 25.9 million went to senior debt, but the preferred dividend of USD 2.2 million for nine months 2026 continues. Two officers hold an interest in OneH2, to which Alta paid USD 5.3 million for a hydrogen plant and which entered creditor assignment in June 2026. Ownership percentages, board detail and the terms of the 2026 investor agreements are not supplied. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is the direction since June 2026: total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.91x to 4.65x, reported availability rose from USD 373.8 million to USD 413.5 million, cover improved from 1.96x at FY2025 to 2.02x, organic revenue fell only 1.0%, and management has cut capital expenditure, stopped dividends and repurchases and sold fleet. No principal is due until 2029, which leaves time to repair earnings. The strongest case for a worse view is that EBITDA has not recovered, the free cash flow gain is not earnings-driven, drawable availability may be smaller than printed limits because the borrowing base is unknown, and cash plus availability covers only 62.82% of the 2029 principal. The view would improve if leverage keeps falling toward the 3.47x of FY2023 with cover above 2.02x and operating cash flow before floor plan changes rises above the USD 89.0 million of the last twelve months. It would worsen if reported availability fell below USD 373.8 million, leverage rose above 4.91x, cover fell below 1.96x, or the borrowing base proved smaller than the printed limits. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

facts.label: Market forces
facts.text: Supplier power is the force that matters most to creditors, and buyer power matters least. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases, suppliers may appoint other distributors, sell direct or end agreements, and their finance arms renew floor plan lines each year, so supplier decisions reach earnings and liquidity. Buyers are fragmented, with no customer above 1% of revenue, and new entrants face OEM exclusivity and a shortage of skilled technicians, so rivalry and substitution are the pressures that show in margins: OEMs discount to win share, which is visible in the 14.07% margin on new and used equipment, and falling rental utilization makes renting a weaker offer for Alta's own fleet. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13, 19, 30, 43–44, 71–72; calculation C9

facts.text: The downside path runs from equipment demand to earnings and then to the 2029 refinancing, and not to near-term liquidity. Softer construction and lift truck demand would cut equipment deliveries and rental utilization, shrink the inventory and receivables that support ABL advances and compress margins; if calculated EBITDA repeated its FY2023 to FY2025 fall of 15.04% from the last-twelve-month level it would be USD 129.8 million, cash interest cover would be 1.72x and total debt to EBITDA 5.48x, or 7.98x counting floor plan payables. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Alta presents an adequate business profile supported by aftermarket-heavy earnings, spread customers and exclusive OEM territories, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 4.65x, cover of 2.02x, a deficit in equity and a single maturity of USD 692.9 million in 2029. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was negative for three years and the recent gain comes from spending cuts and floor plan timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilizing near the current level, on the borrowing base holding and on supplier floor plan lines being renewed. The primary downside path is softer equipment demand that cuts earnings and collateral before the 2029 refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the borrowing base, covenant levels, peer comparison and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the single 2029 maturity of the ABL and second lien notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

spans.text: ## Request

Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings (annual reports for FY2024 and FY2025 and quarterly reports for Q1 to Q3 2026) can support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit analyses, and what remains missing.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five SEC filings are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Alta Equipment Group Inc. to September 30, 2026, giving creditors primary-source debt, liquidity and maturity evidence but no covenant-headroom or intercreditor test, because no credit agreement or indenture was supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–114

Three limits qualify that view. The filings state covenant compliance but print no covenant level, so headroom cannot be measured. Reported borrowing availability of USD 413.5 million is USD 117.4 million below what the printed facility limits imply, and the borrowing base is not printed. Board, ownership and compensation detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. No source document is dated after the November 9, 2026 quarterly report, so the cutoff is respected.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; calculation C3

## Gaps

No executed governing document was supplied. The ABL credit agreement, the floor plan credit agreement and the indenture for the second lien notes due 2029 are described in the notes, and they and the intercreditor agreement are listed as exhibits incorporated by reference, but none is in the source set. No covenant level, definition, basket or springing test is printed in any of the five filings; each report states only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants. No statement separates the issuer, the domestic subsidiary guarantors and the Canadian operations. Covenant headroom, lien priority, guarantor coverage and liability-management capacity therefore cannot be established from these sources. The executed documents named in the exhibit lists would close this gap. Severity: material.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–114

Borrowing availability cannot be reconciled to the printed facility limits. At September 30, 2026 management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities, while the printed combined limit of USD 1,064.5 million less USD 518.9 million outstanding and USD 14.7 million of letters of credit gives USD 530.9 million, a difference of USD 117.4 million. The filings print neither the borrowing base nor the collateral-based limits as amounts that would explain it, so both figures are carried with their roles and neither is chosen. Severity: material.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C2; calculation C3

Governance and ownership detail is incomplete. Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied. The Board Observer Agreement and the Cooperation Agreement with Mill Road Capital III, L.P. dated January 21, 2026 appear only in the exhibit list of the FY2025 annual report, with no terms printed. Severity: minor.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111, 113

No market, rating, peer, portfolio or management-outlook input was supplied. The run settings declare no credit ratings, market quotes, peer set, deal terms or portfolio. None of the filings prints a credit rating level or numerical management guidance; the discussion of results offers qualitative outlook comments only. No current report on Form 8-K or earnings release is in the source set, so events between the November 9, 2026 quarterly report and the November 18, 2026 as-of date cannot be checked. Severity: minor.

The debt perimeter and earnings definitions must be carried by later analysis, not chosen here. Total debt and finance leases of USD 710.7 million exclude floor plan payables (USD 325.7 million carrying amount, presented as current liabilities) and operating lease liabilities (USD 116.0 million). Management's Adjusted EBITDA starts from net loss available to common stockholders, adds back preferred stock dividends and deducts floor plan interest on new equipment, and no covenant EBITDA definition is printed. Proceeds from rent-to-sell equipment sit in operating cash flow while transfers from inventory to the rental fleet are non-cash (USD 97.9 million in the nine months of 2026), so cash flow measures depend on that treatment. Severity: minor.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7–8, 18, 20, 35, 55; calculation C5

Period and version differences must be carried as well. Cash income taxes paid are printed for 2025 (by jurisdiction), 2024 and 2023 in the annual reports but not for the 2026 quarters, whose cash flow statements print cash paid for interest only. The latest debt maturity table is at December 31, 2025; the quarterly reports print maturity dates in text only. The FY2024 annual report corrected the FY2023 and FY2022 cash flow presentation by moving rent-to-rent proceeds of USD 5.4 million and USD 7.5 million from operating to investing cash flow, and the FY2025 annual report carries the corrected FY2023 figures. The FY2024 amounts compared across the two annual reports agree. Severity: minor.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Alta Equipment Group Inc. is a stretched credit: total debt was 4.65x last-twelve-month EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 3.47x at FY2023, and EBITDA covered cash interest only 2.02x, so creditors depend on refinancing the 2029 maturities rather than on deleveraging.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; calculation C82; calculation C80; calculation C85

The ABL facility and the second lien notes, USD 692.9 million together, fall due on the same day in 2029, against cash of USD 21.8 million and reported availability of USD 413.5 million that includes floor plan lines. Counting floor plan payables as debt lifts leverage to 6.78x. Equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million and no covenant level is printed, so headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17–18, 55; calculation C60; calculation C86
### Key findings

Leverage rose because earnings fell while debt grew. Reported EBITDA dropped from USD 192.1 million in FY2023 to USD 159.5 million in FY2024 and was USD 163.2 million in FY2025, while total debt grew from USD 667.0 million to USD 735.0 million, taking total debt to EBITDA from 3.47x to 4.50x. Rental revenues, which cost only USD 20.0 million before depreciation in FY2025, fell from USD 203.4 million to USD 179.8 million and rental equipment sales fell from USD 138.0 million to USD 109.1 million, so the fleet-funded earnings stream is shrinking and creditors hold a larger claim on a smaller earnings base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; calculation C80; calculation C81; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Interest takes about half of EBITDA. Cash interest paid rose from USD 53.6 million in FY2023 to USD 76.4 million in FY2024 and USD 83.4 million in FY2025, so EBITDA cover fell from 3.58x to 1.96x. The last twelve months to September 30, 2026 lifted cover only to 2.02x, because cash interest eased to USD 75.6 million while EBITDA slipped to USD 152.8 million. At cover near 2x a modest earnings decline would cut quickly into the cash left after interest.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C83; calculation C84; calculation C85; calculation C32

Free cash flow after rental and other capital expenditure was an outflow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, of USD 16.2 million, USD 13.5 million and USD 18.0 million. The positive USD 64.2 million over the last twelve months rests on lower capital expenditure, USD 28.5 million against USD 51.0 million in FY2025, and on working capital rather than on higher earnings: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 58.8 million includes a USD 30.8 million inflow from manufacturer floor plan payables, against an outflow of USD 28.3 million in nine months 2025. Floor plan payables are repaid as the financed equipment is sold, so part of the improvement is borrowed and can reverse.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; calculation C50; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C53

Liquidity is adequate in the near term, but how much of it can fund debt service is not established. Cash is USD 21.8 million and management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities combined, and the floor plan facilities primarily finance equipment inventory. The printed facility limits imply USD 530.9 million, USD 117.4 million more than reported, and the filings do not print the borrowing base. No principal falls due before June 2029, when USD 692.9 million of ABL and second lien note principal matures on one day, so a single refinancing decides the credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17–18, 55; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C60

Leverage depends on the debt perimeter. Total debt of USD 710.7 million counts finance leases of USD 32.0 million but not floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million or operating lease liabilities of USD 116.0 million. With floor plan payables counted, total debt to EBITDA is 6.78x rather than 4.65x. The issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA deducts floor plan interest on new equipment as an operating cost, which is consistent with leaving floor plan payables out of debt, so a committee should read 4.65x as the issuer-consistent measure and 6.78x as the conservative bound.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 16–20, 35; calculation C55; calculation C67; calculation C86

Customer deposits and deferred revenue, which fund operations without interest, were USD 33.4 million at September 30, 2026, down from USD 37.8 million at FY2023. The float is small against total debt of USD 710.7 million, so it neither supports liquidity materially nor hides a large claim; the obligation is to deliver equipment or service, and it is not a debt claim.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; calculation C68; calculation C71
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The best case against a harsher view is the direction since June: leverage fell from 4.91x at June 30, 2026 to 4.65x, and net debt fell from USD 716.4 million at FY2025 to USD 688.9 million. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, total debt is 4.38x and cover is 2.15x. No principal falls due before June 2029 and reported availability is USD 413.5 million. The view would improve if leverage keeps falling from 4.65x toward the 3.47x of FY2023 while cover moves above 2.02x, and it would weaken if reported availability fell below the USD 373.8 million of June 30, 2026 or the borrowing base proved smaller than the printed facility limits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 18, 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C87; calculation C88; calculation C66
### Limitations

Reported EBITDA is calculated from net income, interest, tax and depreciation because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, and it adds back floor plan interest that the issuer treats as an operating cost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C73
Interim ratios rest on last-twelve-month figures built from year-to-date statements, and they carry no statement tie.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_altg_altg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5
Covenant levels, the borrowing base and the maturities of individual floor plan facilities are not printed, so covenant headroom and facility-level availability are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18
Cash taxes paid are not printed for the 2026 quarters, and statements before FY2023 are not extracted.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99

## Gaps

Covenant levels, definitions and tests are not printed for any period from FY2023 to September 30, 2026. Every report states only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants. This restricts covenant headroom, any covenant-based liquidity or default analysis and the debt stack's lender tests; no capacity is inferred. The action that would close it is the executed ABL credit agreement, floor plan credit agreement and indenture. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

Borrowing availability cannot be reconciled to the printed facility limits at September 30, 2026. Management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings while the combined limit less borrowings and letters of credit gives USD 530.9 million, a difference of USD 117.4 million, and the borrowing base is not printed. This restricts the undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity chart and every liquidity measure built on it, which carry the reported figure. The action that would close it is the borrowing base certificate or the credit agreement definitions. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C58; calculation C59; Source readiness (CP-0)

The individual floor plan facilities have no printed carrying value, margin, floor or maturity, and the legal rank of the OEM floor plan facilities and of the finance leases is not stated. These instruments therefore carry Not supplied cells in the instrument table and are left out of the debt stack. This restricts any secured-debt subtotal and the ranking of floor plan claims; the action that would close it is the floor plan credit agreements and the intercreditor agreement. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, and the two differ by USD 1.2 million in FY2025 and USD 9.4 million over the last twelve months to September 30, 2026. This restricts every leverage and cover ratio to a labelled basis; the action that would close it is a covenant EBITDA definition, which no supplied document gives. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C72; calculation C73

The debt perimeter is a choice that moves leverage from 4.65x to 6.78x at September 30, 2026: floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million and operating lease liabilities of USD 116.0 million sit outside Total Debt, which follows the issuer's own debt note. This restricts comparison with issuers that count floor plan debt; the action that would close it is a committee decision on the perimeter, with both measures stated. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 16–20; calculation C86; calculation C67

The maturity ladder at September 30, 2026 is built from the instrument terms in the debt note because the quarterly reports print no maturity table; the last printed table is at December 31, 2025, and it holds principal only in 2029. Finance leases are outside the ladder and appear in the reconciling items. This restricts the ladder to ABL and second lien note principal; the action that would close it is a maturity table in a later report. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 20; calculation C60; calculation C61

Cash income taxes paid are not printed for the 2026 interim periods, so cash tax for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 is not established; the annual reports print it for FY2023 to FY2025. This restricts cash-tax-based cash flow measures for 2026; the action that would close it is the cash flow supplemental disclosure in a later report. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

Printed dashes are carried as Not supplied, not as zero, in these lines and periods: other income in Q3 2025; gain or loss on divestitures in FY2023, FY2024, Q1 2025 and Q3 2026; loss on debt extinguishment in FY2023 and FY2025; debt issuance cost and extinguishment lines in FY2023 and FY2025; acquisitions in FY2024, Q1 2026, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; divestiture proceeds in FY2023, FY2024 and Q1 2025; repurchases of common stock in FY2023, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; common dividends in the 2026 periods; and the foreign exchange effect in FY2023 and Q1 2025. Lines a period's statement does not print are likewise Not supplied. The totals tie without them, which indicates nil. This restricts nothing in the ratios; the action that would close it is the issuer's confirmation that a dash means nil. Severity: Low.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–74; 10-Q_2026-03-31_altg_altg-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8

Statements for FY2022, per-share data, share counts and the Q2 discrete quarter are not extracted, and segment assets and segment capital expenditures are not extracted. This restricts the history before FY2023 and the segment return measures; the action that would close it is extraction from the segment note and the FY2024 annual report. Severity: Low.

Operating measures such as rental fleet utilization and backlog are described in words and not quantified, and the preferred stock's liquidation preference is not printed. This restricts operating trend analysis and the ranking of the preferred claim; the action that would close it is management disclosure of those measures. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 48–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 43

No subsequent event is stated in the latest quarterly report, and events between November 9, 2026 and the November 18, 2026 as-of date cannot be checked from the supplied sources. This restricts the post-balance-sheet adjustments to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for that interval. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59

spans.text: ## Request

Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: business model, ownership and control, governance, sponsor and shareholder behaviour, capital allocation and transaction history, drawn from the five supplied SEC filings.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Alta is a diversified, OEM-anchored equipment dealer in which the supplied filings identify no controlling holder or sponsor, so creditors face operating and financial-policy risk more than extraction risk, and governance risk is medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 10–11, 111; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 25

Parts and service are 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit, and no customer exceeds 1% of revenue, which supports cash-flow durability. Against that, distributions of USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025 exceeded the cash left after investment in every year, so they leaned on borrowing, and preferred dividends continue with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million. The chief executive officer and chief financial officer hold an indirect minority interest in OneH2, which Alta paid USD 5.3 million to build a plant and which went into creditor assignment in June 2026; ownership, board and compensation detail is not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40, 71–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C18
### Key findings

The operating model is durable at its core and dependent on suppliers at its edges. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, while new and used equipment sales, 54.43% of revenue, earned a 14.07% margin. Alta is the exclusive distributor of new equipment and replacement parts in substantially all of its territories, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue and the top ten are about 6%, so cash flow is spread across many buyers. The dependency is on the manufacturers: five of them supplied 49% of equipment and parts bought in FY2025, a supplier may terminate a distribution agreement, and OEM finance arms provide floor plan lines that renew each year after a credit review, so one supplier's decision can reach both earnings and liquidity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 13, 19, 30, 71–72; calculation C1; calculation C5

Earnings rest on Construction Equipment, and Material Handling is the weaker segment in 2026. Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue and 59.52% of segment Adjusted EBITDA before corporate costs, at a 9.04% margin. In the first nine months of 2026 Material Handling revenue fell 5.94% and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.01%, as new and used equipment sales dropped 11.67%, while Construction Equipment revenue rose 1.02% but its Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.74%. Reported group revenue fell 1.76%, but the issuer's organic revenue, which removes acquired and divested revenue, fell only 1.0%, to USD 1,302.5 million from USD 1,315.0 million, so nearly half of the reported decline comes from sold businesses. Group Adjusted EBITDA was USD 121.6 million against USD 123.8 million a year earlier, a margin of 9.33% in both periods, so the earnings base is flat to slightly lower and gives creditors no growth cushion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 105–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 35; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7

The rental fleet is being shrunk on purpose, which turns fleet assets into cash at the cost of rental income. Management began a fleet optimization in mid-2024 aimed at excess rent-to-sell assets and weak-return classes, cutting rental fleet gross cost by USD 84.3 million from 2024-06-30 to 2025-12-31 and new equipment inventory by USD 51.5 million in FY2025. Rental revenue fell 11.60% in FY2025 and a further 4.38% in the first nine months of 2026, while rental equipment sales rose 18.42%, so part of the cash generated has come from selling fleet, not from earnings growth. Management describes rental rates as stable to slightly positive, but utilization is not quantified, so how far the fleet cuts have outrun demand is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation C4; calculation C8

No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, which removes sponsor-extraction risk but leaves no named party committed to support the equity. Alta's shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, ownership, board and compensation detail is incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the market value of shares held by non-affiliates implies that affiliates held about 20% of the common shares in mid-2025. An investor, Mill Road Capital III, signed a board observer agreement and a cooperation agreement with Alta on 2026-01-21, but the filings give neither its holding nor the terms. Stockholders' equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million at September 30, 2026, so equity offers no loss-absorbing cushion, and no guarantee, cure right or equity injection by a holder is described in any of the filings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 111, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5–6; calculation C10; calculation C18

Shareholder distributions exceeded the cash left after investment in each of the last three years, so they leaned on borrowing; they have been cut back since, but not ended. Common dividends, preferred dividends and repurchases totalled USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025, 28.03% of operating cash flow, while operating cash flow less capital expenditure plus asset-sale proceeds was negative in two years and only USD 3.7 million in the third. The common dividend was halved in 2025 and none is printed for 2026, and repurchases of USD 5.8 million in FY2024 and USD 7.5 million in FY2025 have stopped, with USD 16.7 million of authorization still open. The preferred dividend continues, USD 2.2 million in the first nine months of 2026, despite the deficit. The filings give neither a reason for the changes nor a funding source, so the cut-back is observed, not committed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 58; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

Corporate activity has shifted from buying to selling, which helps creditors modestly. Alta states that it completed 17 acquisitions since 2020 and describes its growth strategy as historically built on acquisitions, but cash spent on acquisitions was USD 45.6 million in FY2023 and USD 2.7 million in FY2025, with no acquisition cash printed for FY2024. The FY2023 purchases of Burris and Ault were funded, together with working capital and rental fleet growth, from net borrowing of USD 91.3 million under the ABL facility. Three disposals since May 2025 had sale prices of USD 18.0 million, USD 6.4 million and USD 1.5 million, USD 25.9 million in all, and each was allocated to reduce senior debt. The strategy has not been withdrawn, and pro forma earnings and integration results are not disclosed for any purchase, so a return to acquisitions would be a re-leveraging risk that the filings do not size.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 74, 102–103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 30; calculation C13; calculation C15

A related-party hydrogen investment is small but now unresolved. The chief executive officer and chief financial officer together hold an indirect, non-controlling minority interest in OneH2, to which Alta has paid USD 5.3 million to build and commercialize a hydrogen production plant for Alta. OneH2 assigned its assets for the benefit of its creditors on 2026-06-24 and the chief executive officer left its board. The total paid has not risen since the FY2024 report, which expected the plant to be operational in the first half of 2025; the FY2025 report moved that to the first half of 2026, and the 2026 reports give no start-up date. Management reports no indication of impairment and is considering commercialization opportunities, but the recoverable value of the plant and any further payments owed are not stated. Hydrogen fuel purchases from OneH2 were USD 0.6 million in FY2025, USD 1.6 million in FY2024 and USD 0.4 million in FY2023.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C19

Reporting quality is adequate for monitoring, with one past correction and gaps in creditor-specific terms. The auditor's report on the FY2025 statements is dated 2026-02-26, management concluded that internal control over financial reporting was effective, and the FY2024 annual report corrected an error that had put rent-to-rent equipment sale proceeds in operating rather than investing cash flow, overstating operating cash flow by USD 7.5 million in FY2022 and USD 5.4 million in FY2023. The credit agreements, the indenture and the Series A preferred terms are not in the filings, so creditor protections must be taken from documents not supplied. Separately, 23.64% of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, two of which expire in 2027, and one multiemployer pension plan is in the red zone with a rehabilitation plan and a surcharge, a USD 1.7 million annual contribution whose withdrawal liability is not quantified.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 68, 104–105, 108–109; calculation C9; calculation C17

Overall, Alta presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is borrowing-funded distributions that are now curtailed, which matters because every dollar paid out while cash after investment was negative added to the claims that mature together in 2029 and implies a refinancing that depends on cash flow, not on outside support. Countervailing evidence is the stop to common dividends and repurchases, the use of disposal proceeds to repay senior debt and the cut to capital expenditure. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the terms of the 2026 investor agreements and the credit agreements.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 74, 92–93, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 18, 24; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that governance risk is higher than medium is a pattern of paying out cash the business had not generated: distributions of USD 41.6 million over three years, repurchases in loss years, a preferred dividend still paid with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million, and two senior officers holding an interest in a related party that has failed. The strongest case that it is lower is behaviour since mid-2025: common dividends and repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt. The view would worsen on evidence of a holder with control of the vote or a cooperation agreement that favours distributions or a sale, wide restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreements combined with resumed dividends or repurchases, or a further payment to OneH2. It would improve if the proxy statement shows an independent board with no controlling holder, the credit documents block distributions while debt is high, and further quarters pass with no payment beyond the preferred dividend.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 73–74, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 14, 24, 58; calculation C8; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C18
### Limitations

- Without the proxy statement, who holds the common shares and whether any holder can steer distributions or a sale is not established, so the medium rating rests on the absence of a controlling holder in the filings, not on a confirmed share register.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 111; calculation C10

- Without the terms of the January 2026 board observer and cooperation agreements, whether an outside investor has gained influence over capital allocation is not established; terms that commit Alta to a sale process or repurchases would raise the risk level.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113

- The credit agreements and indenture were not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, make investments or add liens is unknown and willingness to distribute is read only from what Alta actually paid; the distribution findings carry no capacity test.

- The hydrogen plant's carrying value and any commitment to OneH2 are not stated, so whether USD 5.3 million is recoverable is not established and the related-party finding is sized only by amounts paid.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Pro forma earnings and integration results for acquisitions, and the liquidation preference and redemption terms of the Series A preferred, are not printed, so acquisition discipline is judged from spending and funding alone and the preferred claim cannot be sized.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 102–103
### Company and operating model
| Operating measure | 9M 2026 | 9M 2025 | Change | Creditor consequence | Source |

| Total revenues | USD 1,303.4 million | USD 1,326.8 million | -1.76% | A flat to lower top line gives no growth to absorb fixed costs or support deleveraging | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |

| Organic revenues, excluding acquired and divested revenue (issuer measure) | USD 1,302.5 million | USD 1,315.0 million | -0.95% (issuer prints -1.0%) | Nearly half of the reported decline is sold businesses; the underlying decline is small | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35 |

| New and used equipment sales | USD 673.0 million | USD 698.4 million | -3.64% | Cyclical and the lowest-margin line, but it seeds the parts and service base | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |

| Parts and service revenues | USD 415.2 million | USD 420.3 million | -1.21% | The stable base, 31.86% of revenue, holds up better than equipment sales | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |

| Rental revenues | USD 131.0 million | USD 137.0 million | -4.38% | Rental income keeps falling after an 11.60% drop in FY2025, as management cuts fleet it judged excess | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 71–72 |
| Rental equipment sales | USD 84.2 million | USD 71.1 million | +18.42% | Fleet sales raise cash while shrinking the earning fleet | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |
| Segment Adjusted EBITDA, total | USD 121.6 million | USD 123.8 million | -1.78% | Earnings are steady at a 9.33% margin in both periods | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |

| Capital expenditures | USD 20.8 million | USD 43.3 million | -51.96% | Spending was cut by half, which preserves cash; fleet age and replacement need are not quantified | 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new debt was issued in FY2025 or in the first nine months of 2026. The last issue was the USD 500.0 million senior secured second lien notes due 2029-06-01, completed on 2024-06-05 to refinance earlier second lien notes due April 2026, with a USD 6.7 million loss on extinguishment, to reduce variable-rate exposure and to provide liquidity and growth funding. On the same day the ABL facility was amended to raise its capacity to USD 520.0 million, including a USD 45.0 million Canadian sublimit, and to extend its maturity to 2029-06-01, and the ABL, floor plan and second lien agents signed an intercreditor agreement. The notes are guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary and secured by second-priority liens on substantially all assets, behind the first-priority liens that secure the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility. At September 30, 2026 USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due in 2029, and the floor plan and ABL facilities together are limited to USD 1,064.5 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93, 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation C16

Other transactions are small. Alta bought the assets of a Quebec Yale dealer for USD 2.7 million on 2025-03-14 and sold three businesses with sale prices of USD 18.0 million (2025-05-01), USD 6.4 million (2025-08-29) and USD 1.5 million (2026-03-01), allocating each set of proceeds to reduce senior debt. The 2023 purchases of Burris, for USD 16.7 million in cash, and Ault, for USD 35.7 million including USD 5.3 million of Alta stock and a USD 3.2 million seller note, were the last large acquisitions, and net ABL borrowing of USD 91.3 million in FY2023 funded them together with working capital and rental fleet growth.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C13; calculation C15

No equity offering, sponsor funding or dividend recapitalization since 2023 is described in the filings. Alta raised its repurchase authorization twice, to USD 20.0 million in October 2024 and to USD 30.0 million in May 2025, and signed board observer and cooperation agreements with Mill Road Capital III on 2026-01-21, whose terms are not supplied. The June 2026 increase in the incentive plan share reserve dilutes equity holders but costs creditors no cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

## Gaps

Ownership percentages by holder, board composition, independence and executive compensation are not supplied, because Part III of the annual report is incorporated from a proxy statement. This restricts the ownership register, the control conclusion and the governance risk level to the absence of a controlling holder in the filings; the action that would close it is the 2026 proxy statement. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 111; calculation C10; Source readiness (CP-0)

The terms and the holding behind the January 2026 board observer and cooperation agreements with Mill Road Capital III are not supplied, because only the exhibit titles appear. This restricts any view on whether an outside investor can influence distributions, repurchases or a sale; the action that would close it is the current report filed on 2026-01-22 and its exhibits. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113

The credit agreements, indenture and intercreditor terms are not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment, lien and asset-transfer capacity cannot be assessed and no sponsor or shareholder willingness is inferred from capacity. This restricts the distribution flags to what Alta actually paid; the action that would close it is the executed documents with basket usage. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93, 113–114; Source readiness (CP-0)

The funding source of dividends and repurchases and the way Alta meets the Delaware test for dividends while equity is negative are not stated. This restricts the finding that distributions leaned on borrowing to an inference from the cash flow statement; the action that would close it is management discussion in the next annual report. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; calculation C12; calculation C13

The carrying value, operating status and commercialization plan of the hydrogen plant, and any commitments to OneH2, are not supplied, and the expected start-up date has slipped from the first half of 2025 to the first half of 2026 with no later date given. This restricts the size of the related-party exposure to amounts paid; the action that would close it is the notes to the next quarterly report. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

Rental fleet utilization and backlog are described in words and not quantified, and the OEM distribution and floor plan agreements are not supplied. This restricts the test of aftermarket and rental durability to reported revenue and gross profit by line, and the supplier-termination risk to the risk factor wording; the action that would close it is earnings materials and the dealer agreements. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32

Pro forma earnings, integration cost and synergy results for acquisitions are not disclosed, and revenue by country is not printed. This restricts any view that acquisitions added earnings and the currency and regional exposure of the revenue base; the action that would close it is acquisition disclosures and a geographic revenue note. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 102

The liquidation preference, redemption terms and dividend-blocking terms of the Series A preferred are not printed, and the multiemployer pension withdrawal liability is not quantified. This restricts the size and ranking of the preferred claim and of the pension contingent claim; the action that would close it is the certificate of designation and plan administrator estimates. Severity: Low.

Events after the latest quarterly report, signed on 2026-11-09, cannot be checked from the supplied sources, and the latest report states no subsequent event. This restricts the events timeline to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for the interval to the as-of date. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59

spans.text: ## Request

Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: the fundamental credit view built from the five supplied SEC filings and the three earlier module handoffs: business quality, leverage, free cash flow, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy, downside path and monitoring.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |
